A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Manual-PA. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete supplementary materials are readable and support matching retained, relocated, and added content.

before.justification: V1 reports original Manual-PA experiments on PartNet and IKEA-Manual, including quantitative comparisons, ablations, and supplementary analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains these original results and adds Multi-Part, Multi-View, and cross-category evaluations.

M1.justification: The core architecture and losses remain unchanged. V2 adds procedural adaptations: grouping similar parts and assigning group positional encodings for Multi-Part, and concatenating separately encoded consecutive diagrams for Multi-View (Appendix D.1). RoPE was already documented and ablated in v1's appendix; its new main-text mention does not establish a new component.

E1.justification: V2 substantially broadens evaluated conditions to multiple parts per step, changing viewpoints, and transfer from chair training to table and storage testing. PartNet storage itself is retained coverage: v1 already evaluated it in Appendix D.1. The underlying datasets remain PartNet and IKEA-Manual.

E2.justification: SPAFormer is added to the storage comparison in v2 Table 1, whereas v1's supplementary Table 4 compared against Image-PA variants. SPAFormer already appeared for chair and table in v1, but its participation in the retained storage experiment is new. Other established comparator sets remain substantially unchanged.

E3.justification: The added experiments introduce substantial new protocols: fine-tuning for grouped assembly steps and changing viewpoints, sampling views from eight cube vertices, inserting an initial blank diagram, and fixing the final viewpoint. Cross-category testing trains on chairs and evaluates other categories. The original benchmark splits, metrics, and standard training settings are retained.

E4.justification: V2 adds tests of adaptation to multiple-part steps and viewpoint changes, plus cross-category generalization. These examine important applicability questions absent from v1's experiments. Existing part-count, attention, order, RoPE, decoder-depth, and permutation-noise analyses are retained or relocated. The explicitly labeled storage ground-truth-order comparison is no longer tabulated.

E5.justification: V2 Table 1 newly states that Multi-View results are averaged over five runs. V1 provides no corresponding run-count report. This does not establish increased repetition of retained experiments, and no seeds, dispersion estimates, confidence intervals, or significance tests are added.

E6.justification: V2 adds Multi-Part and Multi-View results, SPAFormer storage scores, and cross-category findings. Figure 3 reports PA of 83.9 and 56.0 for Manual-PA trained on chairs and tested on table and storage, versus 49.1 and 28.6 for Image-PA. Original benchmark scores are retained; the separately labeled storage ground-truth-order result row is omitted.

T1.justification: Appendix D.1 adds a grouped matching formulation with M part groups and an M-by-M similarity matrix, extending the original individual-part matching assumptions. This is a limited formal extension; the original assignment equations, losses, and metric definitions in Eqs. (1)-(14) remain unchanged, and no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract and central contributions concerning manual-guided order learning and pose estimation remain unchanged. The introduction adds cross-category generalization to the contribution claims, while the conclusion now describes varying part counts per step and viewpoints as addressed capabilities rather than future work.

C2.justification: V2 interprets cross-category performance as evidence that Manual-PA extracts assembly information from manuals instead of relying solely on shape priors. The conclusion replaces the multiple-part and viewpoint limitations with challenges involving arrows, close-ups, and labels, retains nonlinear subassemblies as a limitation, and drops the earlier unified-model future-work statement.

D1.justification: New Appendix D.1 documents fine-tuning, Chamfer-based grouping, viewpoint construction, blank initial diagrams, fixed final views, and feature concatenation. Section 4.1 also supplies the storage part count and explains IKEA storage's exclusion. Existing optimizer settings, training budgets, hardware, training times, and the code/data release promise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds Modeling by Example, ComplementMe, and Coalesce to the semantic-part assembly background. RoFormer additionally appears in the main references but was already cited in v1's supplement. The central positioning relative to previous assembly and pose-estimation research is retained.

P1.justification: Changes are concentrated in the experimental narrative, dataset description, conclusion, and Appendix D. Part-count and attention-map discussions move into the supplement, while storage results receive main-text coverage. Most prose, the method exposition, and the overall section hierarchy remain intact.

P2.justification: Table 1 gains storage columns and Multi-Part/Multi-View rows, absorbing most of the former supplementary storage table. V2 adds the cross-category bar chart as Figure 3 and relocates the part-count and attention-map figures to the appendix. Remaining figures are largely retained, renumbered, or repositioned, including the qualitative examples.

improvement.justification: V2 supplies useful evidence for multiple-part and changing-view conditions that v1 left to future work, and strengthens generalization evidence through cross-category testing. These gains remain limited by constrained synthetic settings and reporting inconsistencies: Figure 3's storage reference PA is 58.1 versus 56.51 in Table 1, without explanation. The broader superiority wording also overlooks SPAFormer's higher storage SR, 7.850 versus Manual-PA's 4.730.
